title: Modals (Models)
content:
Definition

English: Modals are auxiliary verbs that express the mood or attitude of the speaker, such as ability, possibility, permission, or necessity.
Hindi: Modals sahayak kriyaen hoti hain jo vakta ka bhav ya drishtikon vyakt karti hain, jaise kshamata, sambhavana, anumati, ya aavashyakta.

They modify the meaning of the main verb.
Yeh mukhya kriya ke arth ko badalte hain.

Example: She can dance well.
Hindi: Wah accha naach sakti hai.

title: Functions of Modals
content:
Explanation

English: Each modal verb expresses a specific function like ability, permission, obligation, or probability.
Hindi: Har modal kriya ek vishesh karya jaise kshamata, anumati, kartavya, ya sambhavana vyakt karti hai.

Main Functions

  • Ability: 'can', 'could'
  • Permission: 'may', 'can'
  • Obligation: 'must', 'should'
  • Possibility: 'might', 'could'
  • Advice: 'should', 'ought to'
  • Necessity: 'must', 'have to'
Example: You should study hard.
Hindi: Tumhe man laga kar padhai karni chahiye.

title: Modals of Ability
content:
Use

English: Express what someone is able to do.
Hindi: Yeh batate hain ki koi vyakti kya kar sakta hai.

Common Modals

  • Can: Present ability (e.g., I can swim.)
  • Could: Past ability or polite request (e.g., I could dance when I was young.)
Example: He can speak three languages.
Hindi: Wah teen bhaashayen bol sakta hai.

title: Modals of Permission
content:
Use

English: Express asking for or giving permission.
Hindi: Yeh anumati maangne ya dene ke liye upyog hote hain.

Common Modals

  • Can: Informal permission (e.g., Can I leave?)
  • May: Formal permission (e.g., May I come in?)
  • Could: Polite request (e.g., Could I borrow your pen?)
Example: You may go now.
Hindi: Tum ab ja sakte ho.

title: Modals of Obligation
content:
Use

English: Indicate duty, responsibility, or necessity.
Hindi: Yeh kartavya, zimmedari, ya aavashyakta darshate hain.

Common Modals

  • Must: Strong necessity (e.g., You must wear a helmet.)
  • Should: Moral duty or advice (e.g., You should help others.)
  • Have to: External obligation (e.g., I have to pay bills.)
Example: You must obey the rules.
Hindi: Tumhe niyamon ka paalan karna hi hoga.

title: Modals of Possibility
content:
Use

English: Express what is possible or uncertain.
Hindi: Yeh batate hain ki kuch ho sakta hai ya nahi bhi ho sakta.

Common Modals

  • Might: Weak possibility (e.g., It might rain.)
  • May: Reasonable possibility (e.g., It may snow tonight.)
  • Could: General or uncertain possibility (e.g., It could happen.)
Example: He might come tomorrow.
Hindi: Wah kal aa sakta hai.

title: Modals of Advice
content:
Use

English: Used to give suggestions or advice.
Hindi: Salah ya sujhav dene ke liye prayog kiye jaate hain.

Common Modals

  • Should: Suggestion or moral advice (e.g., You should rest.)
  • Ought to: Moral or logical duty (e.g., You ought to respect elders.)
Example: You ought to be careful.
Hindi: Tumhe saavdhan rehna chahiye.

title: Modals of Necessity
content:
Use

English: Show something that is essential or unavoidable.
Hindi: Yeh darshate hain ki kuch aavashyak ya anivaray hai.

Common Modals

  • Must: Personal necessity (e.g., I must finish this work.)
  • Have to: External necessity (e.g., I have to catch the bus.)
Example: We have to submit the form today.
Hindi: Humein aaj form jama karna hai.

title: Common Challenges with Modals
content:
Explanation

English: Learners often confuse modals because some have multiple meanings or change form in the past tense.
Hindi: Seekhne walon ko modals mein kathinai hoti hai kyunki kuch modals ke kai arth hote hain ya ve past tense mein badal jaate hain.

Example: 'Can' becomes 'could' in the past, but 'must' has no past form.
Hindi: 'Can' ka past 'could' hota hai, lekin 'must' ka koi past form nahi hota.
